issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the theory covers diagonal/adaptive and curvature-aware preconditioners. Every result analyzes one fixed deterministic SPD matrix M (update \eqref{alg:PSGD} with constant M; "Fix an SPD matrix $\bfM$" in the local section), with all constants (M-strong convexity, M-Lipschitz gradient, moment bounds in the fixed M^{-1}-norm) defined in that one metric. Adaptive methods (Adam, RMSProp, AdaGrad) and the curvature-aware methods used in the experiments (Hessian, GGN/Fisher, K-FAC, L-BFGS) use iterate-dependent, random, time-varying preconditioners M_k; no assumption or proof is stated for such M_k, and the descent/noise estimates do not transfer.

failure_location.quote: The theory covers diagonal/adaptive and curvature‑aware preconditioners.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Requalify the claim to fixed SPD preconditioners (including fixed diagonal and fixed curvature-based M) and present adaptive/state-dependent methods as a design heuristic, or add a new analysis for random time-varying M_k with correspondingly strengthened assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope — that the rate, noise-floor and basin-stability theory applies to adaptive and curvature-based optimizers — is unsupported; only fixed SPD preconditioners (e.g. the fixed spectral M of the diagnostic experiment) fall under the theorems.
issues.title: Claimed coverage of adaptive and curvature-based preconditioners unsupported
issues.why_classification: A short re-qualification preserves every theorem, rate and floor bound, but necessarily withdraws the advertised regime of adaptive/state-dependent preconditioners; establishing that regime would require a new analysis with new assumptions.

issues.failure_explanation: For twice differentiable F, M-Lipschitz continuity of the gradient with constant L̂ is equivalent to ||P^T∇²F(w)P||_2 ≤ L̂ for all w, i.e. to eigenvalues in [−L̂, L̂]; a one-sided bound λ ≤ L̂ is not equivalent without a PSD/convexity hypothesis. E.g. f(z) = −z²/2 (equivalently F(w) = −(w^T M^{-1} w)/2) has its only eigenvalue −1 ≤ L̂ = 0 yet its gradient is 1-Lipschitz, not 0-Lipschitz. The proof's step equating Lipschitz continuity with "eigenvalues bounded above" silently uses positivity of the Hessian, which is not among the lemma's hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "eigenvalues ≤ L̂" by "eigenvalues bounded in absolute value by L̂" (or add a convexity/PSD-Hessian hypothesis) in the lemma, its restatement and the remark.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lemma:bound(i), its verbatim restatement lem:added-1 and Remark rmk:condNum are false as stated for nonconvex F; downstream strongly convex results are unaffected because Assumption assumption:44 forces the relevant eigenvalues to be positive.
issues.title: Spectral characterization of M-Lipschitz gradient uses a one-sided eigenvalue bound
issues.why_classification: A one-clause local correction of a characterization; every conclusion, rate, floor and guarantee of the paper survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimate is only an upper bound whose right-hand side tends to C, so at best limsup E[F(w_k)−F_*|τ=∞] ≤ C follows. Convergence to C is false whenever the variance bound is not saturated along the trajectory: for F(w)=w²/2 with g = w+ζ, ζ = ±a unbiased (so K = a² is the minimal admissible noise level, μ = μ̂_PL = α_QG = L̂ = K_G = 1, PL/QG/containment all hold, P(τ=∞)=1 for a ≤ r), the iterates form an AR(1) with E[F(w_k)] → ᾱa²/(2(2−ᾱ)) = C/(2−ᾱ) < C.

issues.failure_explanation: Ω_∞ = {τ = ∞} depends on ξ_k and later noise and is not F_k-measurable, so the one-step inequality E[S_{k+1}|F_k] ≤ … cannot be restricted to Ω_∞ (nor multiplied by 1_{Ω_∞}) to yield E[S_{k+1}|F_k, Ω_∞] ≤ … : such conditioning changes the conditional law of g_k used to derive the inequality. Hence the recursions x_{k+1} ≤ (1−ρ)x_k + ρC and x_{k+1} ≤ (1−a/(γ+k))x_k + b/(γ+k)² for x_k = E[F(w_k)−F_*|τ=∞] do not follow. What the stopped-process estimates do give is the same bounds for the unconditioned sub-expectations E[(F(w_k)−F_*)1_{k<τ}].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid estimate for the survival-conditioned recursion (e.g. a weighted/Doob h-transform supermartingale argument), or weaken the statements to E[F(w_k)−F_*|τ=∞] ≤ (C+(1−ρ)^{k−1}(F(w_1)−F_*−C))/P(τ=∞) (resp. ν/((γ+k)P(τ=∞))), which follows from the stopped-process estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional geometric and O(1/k) convergence conclusions of thm:3rdmainthm and thm:4thmainthm are unproved, and are not even well defined in cases allowed by the hypotheses (P(τ=∞) can be 0).
issues.title: Survival-conditioned rate bounds condition on a non-measurable event
issues.why_classification: The inference is genuinely invalid; a repair needs a contained new argument (weighted supermartingale) or a limited weakening by a factor 1/P(τ=∞), while the rate form and floor constant remain recognizable.

issues.failure_explanation: E[Y_{k+1}|F_k] ≤ (1−ρ1_{k<τ})Y_k does not imply E[Y_{k+1}|F_k] ≤ Y_k: when Y_k < 0, i.e. F(w_k)−F_* < C (in particular at the minimizer), (1−ρ)Y_k > Y_k, so Y is not a supermartingale and optional stopping is unavailable. In thm:4thmainthm the analogous step "≤ Y_k" requires F(w_k)−F_* ≥ (α_k/α_1)C̃, which is neither assumed nor true. The claimed bound is itself false: with F(w)=w²/2, M=1, r=1, r_+=3, g = w+ζ and ζ ∈ {0,±2,±4} with probabilities 0.96, 0.01, 0.01 (μ = μ̂_PL = α_QG = L̂ = μ_G = K_G = 1, K = 0.4), all of Assumptions localPL–onestep hold and ᾱ = 1/2 satisfies every learning-rate restriction in the theorem, yet from w_1 = 0 ∈ S the first update leaves N_r with probability 0.02 at each visit to S, so P(τ = ∞) = 0 while the theorem asserts P(τ = ∞) ≥ 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the noise-independent infinite-horizon lower bound by a guarantee that accounts for noise-induced single-step exits (e.g. a finite-horizon bound carrying the K term) or add an assumption forbidding exits from N_r in one step, and give a valid optional-stopping argument for the shifted process.
issues.overall_effect: The basin-stability guarantees of thm:3rdmainthm and thm:4thmainthm — advertised in the abstract, the contributions and the conclusion as an explicit lower bound on the probability of remaining in the basin — are false under the stated assumptions: survival probability can be zero even when F(w_1) = F_*. All prose restatements of this guarantee inherit the defect.
issues.title: Basin-stability lower bound on P(τ=∞) is false
issues.why_classification: A counterexample satisfying every hypothesis falsifies the bound, and under the stated assumptions P(τ=∞) may be 0 even from the minimizer, so no comparable noise-free infinite-horizon guarantee survives; any fix changes either the guarantee type or the assumption regime.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 1 gives only an upper bound converging to the floor ᾱL̂K/(2ĉμ) with per-step factor (1−ᾱĉμ); it does not show that the gap ever drops strictly below that floor (indeed the bound increases to the floor when F(w_1)−F_* is below it, and unbiased noise makes the gap rise from 0 to the floor). Nor is the guaranteed rate ĉ/L̂: in the corollary's setting (unbiased gradients with gradient-independent variance) K_G = 1, so the admissible step is ᾱ ≤ 1/L̂ and the contraction factor is 1−ᾱĉ, while ᾱĉ ≤ ĉ/L̂ is only an upper bound on the per-step improvement obtained at the largest admissible step.
